correctness.rationale: Real and imaginary parts give exactly n distinct line restrictions. Each is a real degree-n polynomial with a real Kostlan degree-m limit. A scaling identity gives the full set of n-m nonzero escaping-root limits, and simple-root continuity rigorously counts real versus nonreal branches. The leading Gaussian coefficient has uniform phase, so a cyclic cosine grid yields exact outer count, mean n and parity-resonance variance. Kac–Rice integration gives exactly \(\sqrt m\) expected finite real roots on every line. Uniform n^2 boundedness justifies dominated convergence, and exact simple-root parity yields the claimed integer existential bound, including (77,5). Six exact rational Sturm examples, 4,730 finite phase-grid checks and the arithmetic corollary pass; these are independent corroborative finite tests, not the infinite proof. Residual risk: unknown priority, not correctness under the stated assumptions.

originality.rationale: The closest full text, Lundberg arXiv:2201.00788, introduced exactly the same coupled Kostlan construction but only established ceil(\(n\sqrt m\)) by bounded-interval root persistence (Section 3, Lemma 3.2); Sections 3-4 do not count the infinity branches or present the new bound. The full Khavinson–Lee–Saez 2018 paper exhibits degree-raising perturbative creation of roots in a different family; it does not supply the Gaussian phase-grid distribution or the \(n(1+\sqrt m)\) inequality. Both standard root continuity and the Kostla\(n\sqrt m\) mean are expressly treated as known ingredients. Targeted research-record searches and own accessible claims revealed no covering statement. Novelty remains subject to specialist historical verification. Hauenstein et al. (2014) was additionally inspected in full for its small-degree tables and distinct random models.
residual_risks: Historical priority: an unindexed or differently phrased real-root perturbation theorem could imply the new expected count or the sharper \(m=5\) corollary.

Root creation under degree-raising perturbation is classical and explicitly present in 2018 literature; only the coupled Gaussian mean, arithmetic outer-count distribution and strengthened valence consequence are claimed as new.
This is a self-review; no independent mathematical validation or literature audit has been conducted.

value.rationale: The exact order-n gain over the motivating probabilistic lower bound matters to a natural degree-indexed extremal invariant, establishes a whole-degree-range lower bound yielding a degree-\((77,5)\) violation of the historical equality (without claiming that degree \(5\) was untouched by other constructions) and establishes a complete gcd-controlled deterministic-versus-two-point outer-root law. The finding connects ordinary root perturbations to the zero count of a coupled Gaussian harmonic polynomial and clarifies an entire missing asymptotic root population, not an arbitrary sample statistic.
